The multilingual evidence confirms the split decisively — Spanish uses 'invierno' for the season but 'tempestad' for the storm, and English shifts from 'winter' to 'storm.'"

Spanish 'invierno / en invierno,' Hindi 'jade mein / sardi,' French 'hiver,' and German 'Winter' all converge on the seasonal meaning.
